name: The Chariot
upright: A rehearsed team that detects fast, contains without destroying evidence, recovers, fixes the root cause and learns.
reversed: Panic in the chariot: no plan, the plug pulled on live evidence, no escalation, and the same breach back next month.
vision: A charioteer races through the night with no reins, steering only by a map they drew before ever leaving the stable. A black sphinx strains toward a giant power switch on the city wall while a white sphinx pulls toward the open market; the charioteer drives both into a cage by the roadside. The starry canopy is made of glowing memory that one flick of that switch would erase, so the charioteer scoops each star into a jar first. Each wheel has seven spokes, and each spoke shouts its word as it passes the top: detect, respond, mitigate, report, recover, remediate, learn. At the finish line a scribe writes down every bump in the road.
decode: No reins, only a map drawn in the stable → preparation: the plan, the CSIRT and its escalation and communication paths exist before the incident.
Both sphinxes driven into the cage → containment (ISC2: mitigation): isolate the system, neither switching it off nor leaving it on the network.
Stars of memory scooped into jars → collect volatile data such as RAM, processes and connections first, following the order of volatility.
Seven shouting spokes → the ISC2 steps, in order: detection, response, mitigation, reporting, recovery, remediation, lessons learned.
The scribe at the finish line → lessons learned (NIST: post-incident activity): review the response and feed improvements back into the plan.
facts: NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 has four phases: preparation; detection and analysis; containment, eradication and recovery; and post-incident activity.
In the ISC2 steps, mitigation contains the incident; remediation comes after recovery and finds the root cause so the incident cannot recur.
An event is any observable occurrence; an incident is an event that harms confidentiality, integrity or availability. Every incident is an event, not the reverse.
trap: The collective still flinches toward the power button. Pulling the plug wipes memory and destroys evidence; isolate the system from the network, capture volatile data, then follow the plan.
